items.title: Students cannot be threatened for questioning, dissent is essential to democracy: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan
items.summary: Students cannot be threatened with punitive action for expressing a different point of view or asking questions, Supreme Court Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said on Sunday. Right to question is an essential part of citizenship, liberty and constitutional responsibility, Justice Bhuyan underscored. He was delivering the convocation address at the 13th convocation of National Law University Delhi for its postgraduate programmes. In his address, he spoke on the importance of dissent, tolerance and independent thought in a constitutional democracy, particularly within universities. “In a democracy, the right to question is not an act of defiance. It is an essential expression of citizenship, liberty and constitutional responsibility. So when students express a different point of view, when students ask questions, they cannot be threatened. They cannot be threatened with punitive action. That is unconstitutional. That is misuse of power and office,” he stated. Justice Ujjal Bhuyan When students express a different point of view, when students ask questions, they cannot be threatened with punitive action. The judge said that the Constitution does not seek uniformity of thought, but creates a framework within which people holding different beliefs, opinions and convictions can live with equal dignity and participate in democratic life. He emphasised that tolerance of disagreement is essential to democracy. “A democratic society cannot be built on the edifice that everyone will think alike. items.title: Why has no ‘distinguished jurist’ been made Supreme Court judge in 76 years? Justice Ujjal Bhuyan asks
items.summary: Supreme Court Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Sunday called for a debate on the appointment of distinguished jurists as judges of the Supreme Court. He highlighted that the constitutional provision enabling such appointments has remained unused for over 76 years Justice Bhuyan was delivering the convocation address at the 13th Convocation of National Law University Delhi (NLU Delhi) for its postgraduate programmes. Article 124(3) of the Constitution permits the appointment of a person who is, in the opinion of the President, a distinguished jurist, as a Supreme Court judge. However, Justice Bhuyan pointed out that no jurist has been appointed to the Supreme Court under this provision so far. He suggested two possible reasons for this. “The first is that earlier, when the collegium system was not there, in the view of the Central Government, and thereafter, when the collegium system came into being, in the view of the collegium, there is not enough depth in Indian academia to be seriously considered for elevation as a judge of the Supreme Court,” he said. Justice Bhuyan then offered what he considered the more probable explanation. “The second, which is more probable, is that both the Central Government and the collegium have not seriously explored this provision thus far.” The judge traced the provision to the Constituent Assembly Debates and recalled that HV Kamath had proposed expanding the pool of eligible candidates beyond judges and advocates to include distinguished jurists. The proposal was ultimately accepted by the Constituent Assembly. “The Constituent Assembly evidently felt it important to have legal academics and professors as judges of the Supreme Court of India,” Justice Bhuyan said. He rejected the argument that academics should not be appointed as judges because they lack practical experience. He termed it a "shallow objection". “A distinguished jurist can be a great value addition to the Bench. By his or her scholarship, he or she can make a visible contribution to the decision-making process at the top level,” he said. Justice Bhuyan also referred to constitutional scholar DD Basu’s view that bringing academic jurists of the right calibre into the highest court would enrich it. “It is regrettable that this provision has remained one of our Constitution’s unused mandates.” Justice Bhuyan went on to cite the appointment of academics to constitutional courts in jurisdictions including the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Kenya. items.title: ‘Murderer should not give my daughter a prize’: Father confronts IAS officer Sriram
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A parent in Kerala’s Kozhikode refused to let his daughter receive a prize from IAS officer Sriram Venkitaraman, calling him a “murderer” during a children’s swimming event on Sunday, August 30. The incident took place at a sports complex in Cherootty Nagar, where Sriram Venkitaraman, who currently serves as Director of the Department of Agricultural Development and Farmers’ Welfare, had been invited to distribute prizes to the winners. A video aired by Malayalam news channels showed organisers asking the IAS officer to hand over an award to one of the children. The child’s father refused to accept it on her behalf, repeatedly shouting, “A murderer should not give a prize to my daughter.” Sriram subsequently stepped away, after which the Sub-Collector distributed the awards. IAS officer Sriram is an accused in the 2019 death of journalist KM Basheer. The incident has continued to draw opposition from journalists in Kerala. In June, journalists protested Sriram’s presence at a press conference convened by Agriculture Minister T Siddique. They objected to attending a press conference alongside the officer accused in the death of their former colleague. Following their protest, Sriram left the media room and the press conference resumed. Basheer, 35, who was the Thiruvananthapuram bureau chief of Malayalam daily Siraj, was killed after being struck by a car in the early hours of August 3, 2019. The incident was initially reported as a road accident. Investigators later alleged that Sriram, who was driving a car belonging to a female friend, was under the influence of alcohol when he rammed into Basheer’s motorcycle. Sriram was charged under Section 304 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) for culpable homicide not amounting to murder, along with charges related to negligent and dangerous driving under the Motor Vehicles Act. The case has been under trial for nearly seven years. The next phase of hearings is scheduled from August 1 to September 10.

items.title: Karnataka minister calls Islam superior to other religions, sparks BJP backlash
items.summary: Karnataka Higher Education Minister Basavaraj Rayareddy has triggered a political controversy after describing Islam as "superior to all other religions" while addressing a mass marriage ceremony in Kukanur, Koppal district, held to mark Prophet Muhammad's birth anniversary. Rayareddy said Islam was a "great religion" that promoted humanity and was "scientific in nature," teaching people how to live without becoming religious fanatics or casteists. It is unclear when the event was held. He said many misconceptions were being spread about Islam and that he was willing to study the Quran, adding that the text was meant for all of humanity and not just Muslims. The minister also said he wished to undertake the Hajj pilgrimage but had not had the opportunity to do so, noting that one had to convert to Islam. He said he rarely visits mutts or temples himself, though he tries to study the history of different religions, including Abrahamic faiths. Rayareddy clarified that good principles exist in all religions and that similar practices are followed in temples as well. He also addressed funding for Shadi Mahals (wedding halls), stating that the government provides the funds and that no money comes from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan or other Muslim countries. He added that taking away offerings or land belonging to any religious institution, regardless of faith, was a "great sin." The remarks drew a sharp response from the BJP, which demanded that Chief Minister DK Shivakumar direct Rayareddy to either apologise to the Hindu community or step down from the Cabinet. Karnataka BJP chief R Ashoka accused the minister of demeaning Hinduism and "Sanatan Dharma" through his comments about not frequenting temples and mutts. Taking to X, Ashoka questioned the Congress government's stance, referring to Shivakumar's own frequent temple visits and accusing the government of an "anti-Hindu mindset." He said the Chief Minister stayed silent when his own ministers made "derogatory statements" about Hindu faith centres. Ashoka said Rayareddy's remarks belittled the faith of millions of Hindus and demanded his resignation if he failed to offer an apology.

items.title: Nepal warns of possible fresh flooding as communities grapple with devastation
items.summary: Authorities in Nepal warned of possible fresh flooding on Sunday and urged residents in flood-affected districts to remain on high alert after water levels rose in the Bhotekoshi River. Flood warning notices were sent to people's phones early Sunday as rescue crews worked to clear a major highway connecting Kathmandu to one of the areas worst hit by Wednesday's catastrophic floods, which killed at least 800 people and left more than 3,000 missing in Nepal and Tibet. The latest warnings came after Chinese authorities informed their Nepalese counterparts of increased water flow upstream, according to Dharam Raj Uprety, chief executive of Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority. The Chinese state news agency Xinhua, citing the country's water resources ministry, said a new lake formed after Wednesday's floods high in the mountains had largely drained. But Xinhua said the ministry warned that a crater located 5.6 kilometers (3.5 miles) upstream, which held an estimated 1.4 million cubic meters (370 million gallons) of water, still posed some risk and required close monitoring. Nepal's disaster agency said Sunday the death toll had climbed to 788 with 2,502 missing, while Chinese authorities reported 16 deaths and 546 missing on the Chinese side of the border. The missing include hundreds of people from over a dozen countries who were in the region to work, visit the mountains or make a pilgrimage to a sacred peak. On Sunday, Chinese state media said 261 foreigners were missing in Tibet, including over a hundred Nepalis and others from around the world. Some are returning to what remained of their homes In Dhading, one of the worst-hit regions in Nepal, some residents began returning to ruined homes to see what can be salvaged. Others scanned the ground for items they could pick out of the mud and rinse off. One man had returned for his chickens, which he found alive. He tied them up and put them in the cabin of his truck. "Everything is finished. Nothing is left. Not even our home," Sharmila Tamang, a Dhading resident who was trying to salvage items from her home, told The Associated Press. items.title: Nepal-China flood survivors reach safe areas as families await news of nearly 3,000 missing
items.summary: As rescue efforts in communities buried by catastrophic flash floods along the Nepal - China border entered their fourth day Saturday, authorities were still finding survivors and transporting them to safety. At relief centers, families of missing people waited anxiously for news of their loved ones as the death toll and the number of people unaccounted for continued to rise. The combined toll in Nepal and Tibet rose to 691 dead and over 3,000 people missing after China's latest update on Sunday. Chinese authorities reported 16 deaths and 546 missing, while Nepal's disaster agency said late Saturday that the death toll had climbed to 675 with 2,498 people missing. More than 3,700 people have been rescued in Nepal so far. In Nuwakot, one of the Nepali districts devastated by the floods, helicopters arrived loaded with boxes and bags of aid, including clothes, instant noodles, crackers and rice. Others returned from the flood-hit areas carrying survivors. An older man was carefully helped off one helicopter, while a soldier carried an older woman on his back to a medical tent. Most arrived with nothing except the clothes they were wearing. About a dozen people emerged from another helicopter. Soldiers carried several babies who had been evacuated. The evacuees had been brought from the nearby community of Trishuli. Villagers return to devastated homes As people were still leaving Trishuli, some village residents were returning to see what could be salvaged from their decimated homes. One boy walked out of the village carrying muddy sandals from his house. Another woman, Shoba Shretha, returned to find Sweetie, the dog she was forced to leave behind when the floods came. Shretha sat on the ground petting her and feeding her water from a bottle. At some point, relief coordinators cleared villagers, reporters and volunteers from the entrance to Trishuli, as excavation equipment drove into the flooded village to dig. Families begin to lose hope In Kathmandu, Nepal's capital, relatives and friends gathered outside the main government hospital from early morning, desperately searching for news of missing loved ones. Many shuffled between the help desk and the hospital notice board, clutching photographs and scanning injured patients' lists in the hope of finding them. items.title: Tamil Nadu: Congress warns of Cabinet exit if TVK rejects Rahul as 2029 PM face
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Tamil Nadu Tourism Minister S Rajesh Kumar on Sunday, August 30, warned that the two Congress ministers in the state Cabinet, would quit their posts if ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) refuses to accept Rahul Gandhi as the prime-ministerial candidate for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. Speaking at a Congress party event in Kanniyakumari district, Rajesh Kumar said Rahul Gandhi would be the party’s prime ministerial candidate and the Congress cadres wanted to see him become the next Prime Minister. “If at all TVK refuses to accept this, the two Congress ministers will walk out of the Cabinet,” he said. Rajesh Kumar also said that his party was more important to him than his ministerial post. “If the party asks us to withdraw from the ministry, we will step down the very next minute,” he said. The five MLAs of Congress remain crucial to the TVK-led government’s majority in the Tamil Nadu Assembly. In return, TVK has allotted two ministerial berths to Congress — Tourism to Rajesh Kumar and Higher Education to P Viswanathan. The Congress minister’s remarks came amid attempts by TVK leaders to project Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay as a possible prime ministerial candidate from Tamil Nadu in the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. The issue gained prominence after Public Works Department Minister Aadhav Arjuna, during the Assembly debate on the delimitation exercise, said that a Prime Minister should emerge from Tamil Nadu. Subsequently, other TVK ministers, including D Sarathkumar, A Srinath, and K Jagadeeswari, also spoke about Vijay as a possible PM face. The claims gained wider attention after India Today cited a survey which said Vijay to be the third most preferred choice for Prime Minister in the country, after incumbent Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi. Reacting to TVK leaders’ remarks of projecting Vijay as PM face, Tamil Nadu Congress Committee president (TNCC) Manickam Tagore had stated that they were still behaving with a “fan club mindset.” Earlier on Sunday, Viswanathan was also asked about the number of prime ministerial candidates in the TVK-led alliance at Trichy airport. “Rahul Gandhi is the sole prime ministerial candidate of the Indian National Congress. There will be no change in our stand,” Viswanathan said.

items.title: Close-range shots, multiple wounds: Post mortems contradict Karnataka forest ‘encounter’ claim
items.summary: The autopsies of two of the three people killed by Karnataka Forest Department officials in the Chikkallur reserved forest area on suspicion of being poachers suggest that they were shot from close range, possibly a distance of less than one foot and up to two feet. Preliminary wound ballistics findings in the autopsy report and the fact that the firearm used was a shotgun raise questions about the Forest Department’s claims that the men were shot in self-defence. These claims were repeated in the Legislative Assembly by Forest Minister Ramalinga Reddy. Anthony Swamy, John Rose Peter and Sebastian David Kumar were shot dead in Chikkallur inside the Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary in Hanur taluk in the early hours of August 15. A fourth man, Joseph Mahima Das, later released a video disputing the Forest Department’s account of the incident.
